qa_pairs.question: When does the standard add/drop period end for Fall 2026, and what is the census date?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: For Fall 2026, the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28. The census date is September 4.

contexts.text: For Fall 2026, priority registration opens on July 20, regular registration closes on August 14, classes begin on August 17, and the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28. The census date is September 4.

qa_pairs.question: What is the undergraduate tuition rate for the 2026-2027 academic year?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Undergraduate tuition for the 2026–2027 academic year is USD 420 per registered credit.

contexts.text: Undergraduate tuition for the 2026–2027 academic year is USD 420 per registered credit.

qa_pairs.question: What is the minimum attendance threshold, and can a syllabus change it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold but it may not set a lower threshold.

contexts.text: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold.

qa_pairs.question: How many verified hours are required for an internship, and what is needed before starting?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Programmes with an internship requirement require at least 240 verified hours. Before starting, the student must have an approved placement agreement and workplace supervisor.

contexts.text: Programmes with an internship requirement require at least 240 verified hours. Before starting, the student must have an approved placement agreement and workplace supervisor.

qa_pairs.question: What is the normal undergraduate credit load in Fall/Spring and Summer, and what is required to register above 18 credits?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring and no more than 9 credits in Summer. Registration above 18 credits requires a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20 and written approval from the programme director.

contexts.text: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring and no more than 9 credits in Summer. Registration above 18 credits requires a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20 and written approval from the programme director.

qa_pairs.question: What approvals and fees are needed for a late add, and what happens if I do not pay on time?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.

contexts.text: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.

qa_pairs.question: How much tuition is reversed if I drop a course during standard add/drop, after standard add/drop through census, and after census?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

contexts.text: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal.

qa_pairs.question: Will dropping below 12 graded credits on the census date affect my scholarship?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Yes, dropping below 12 graded credits on or before the census date triggers an immediate eligibility review for the scholarship.

contexts.text: Dropping below 12 graded credits on or before the census date triggers an immediate eligibility review.

qa_pairs.question: Does an approved medical leave use up my one-term scholarship probation opportunity?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No, an approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity.

contexts.text: A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms.
An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity.

qa_pairs.question: What is the timeline to file a formal grade appeal, and what are the permitted grounds?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication. Permitted grounds are calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not permitted.

contexts.text: A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

qa_pairs.question: What should I do if I suspect my portal account is compromised, and will staff ever ask for my password?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: If you suspect account compromise, you should change the password from a trusted device, revoke active sessions, and contact the IT Service Desk. Staff will never request a password or one-time authentication code.

contexts.text: Staff will never request a password or one-time authentication code. A student who suspects account compromise should change the password from a trusted device, revoke active sessions, and contact the IT Service Desk.

qa_pairs.question: Does a financial hold erase my completed academic requirements or prevent me from graduating?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved.

contexts.text: A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`.

qa_pairs.question: I discussed a late-add request in July 2026 but submitted it on August 5, 2026. Which policy version and fee apply?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0, even if first discussed in July. Version 2.0 charges a USD 40 late-add fee per course.

contexts.text: Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.

qa_pairs.question: Does the 5-day grace period for the account balance extend the registration deadline, and what happens if the balance remains unpaid?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The five-calendar-day grace period does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines. An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed.

contexts.text: A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance, but it does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines.

An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed.

qa_pairs.question: If I am approved for a retroactive medical withdrawal after census, how is my tuition and scholarship adjusted?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated.

contexts.text: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and requires the process in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated.

Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation.

qa_pairs.question: What happens if I fail the scholarship renewal requirements a second consecutive time, and can I appeal it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term. Scholarship decisions may be appealed within ten business days to the Financial Aid Review Committee.

contexts.text: A second consecutive failed review ends the award beginning with the next term.
Scholarship decisions may be appealed within ten business days using the process in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.
Scholarship decisions use the same ten-business-day filing window but go to the Financial Aid Review Committee.

qa_pairs.question: What are the conditions for an 'I' incomplete grade, and if it converts to an 'F', can I still graduate?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An 'I' grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing, and an incomplete plan is signed. If it converts to an 'F', it may prevent graduation if the course is a programme requirement, as students must complete all programme-required courses and maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.

contexts.text: An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan.
If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.

An undergraduate student is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.
